main_issue: Whether and how strong-smelling cooking (e.g. D's fish curry) can continue in the shared flat given smell on laundry/rooms, with options of timing, window/door, or notice to move laundry

A-B.evidence: A asks for no strong-smelling cooking (T1); B backs the complaint (T2) but later proposes window/door mitigation (T10, T29) rather than a ban; A never responds to it.

A-C.evidence: C supports the complaint (T3) and insists smell can't be avoided if cooked here (T25, T30), which is in line with A's ban, but A is silent after T5.

A-D.evidence: D offers weekends/not evenings (T4); A accepts: 'Weekends work... after 7pm fine. Thanks, Agent D' (T5); D says 'Okay' (T6). A's original no-strong-smell demand is softened.

B-C.evidence: B and C agree time doesn't help (T8-9), but C rejects B's window/door idea (T11, T30) while B insists it's the only option (T29).

B-D.evidence: D's notice plan accepted by B (T14 'That works'); B's window/door fix is the approach D is exploring; B argued time irrelevant (T8) yet they converge on notice plus window.

C-D.evidence: D proposes notice (T12) and asks for solutions (T22, T26); C rejects them: 'There isn't anywhere else' (T17), 'I don't see a way around it' (T25), 'doesn't stop the smell' (T30).
